heading_en: Credit Risk-Weighted Assets of Original Assets
summary_ja: オリジネーターが資産譲渡型証券化取引でリスク移転・隔離等の条件を満たさない場合は原資産の信用リスク・アセットを算出する旨と、合成型証券化取引等での扱いを定める。
summary_en: Sets out the conditions an originator must meet in an asset-transfer securitization to be relieved from calculating credit RWA on the original assets, and the treatment of synthetic securitizations, early amortization provisions and clean-up calls.
paragraphs: Where an Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. is the originator of an asset-transfer securitization transaction and does not satisfy any one of the following conditions, it shall calculate the amount of credit risk-weighted assets relating to the original assets. (i) The significant credit risk relating to the original assets has been transferred to a third party. (ii) The Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. does not have effective control over the original assets, the original assets are legally isolated from the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. so that neither the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. nor its creditors can exercise control over them even in insolvency proceedings, etc. of the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc., and an opinion of an appropriate attorney, etc. (meaning an attorney under the provisions of the Attorney Act (Act No. 205 of 1949) or a foreign lawyer provided in Article 2, item (iii) of the Act on Special Measures concerning the Handling of Legal Services by Foreign Lawyers (Act No. 66 of 1986); the same applies hereinafter) regarding that state of affairs is held. In this case, where the requirements of (a) or (b) below are satisfied, it is deemed to have effective control: (a) The Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. has a right to repurchase the original assets from the transferee; provided, however, that this does not apply where the exercise of the repurchase right is a clean-up call that satisfies all of the conditions listed in item (vi)(a) through (c). (b) The Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. bears the credit risk relating to the original assets; provided, however, that this does not preclude the holding of a subordinated portion to the extent not contrary to the preceding item. (iii) The rights of investors in the securitization exposures in the securitization transaction do not include a claim against the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. that is the transferor of the original assets. (iv) The transferee of the original assets is a securitization special purpose entity, and the holders of equity interests in that securitization special purpose entity have the right to freely pledge or transfer those equity interests. (v) The contract for the transfer of the original assets does not contain any of the provisions listed in (a) through (c) below: (a) A provision obliging the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. to exchange assets constituting the underlying assets of the securitization exposure for the purpose of improving the credit quality of the original assets; provided, however, that this does not preclude selling the original assets to an independent unrelated third party at market value. (b) A provision permitting the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. to assume additional first-loss positions or credit enhancement after the transfer date. (c) A provision increasing the payment of benefits to investors, third-party credit enhancement providers or any other person than the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. in accordance with the deterioration of the credit quality of the underlying assets of the securitization exposure. (vi) Where the securitization transaction includes a clean-up call, the clean-up call satisfies all of the conditions listed in (a) through (c) below: (a) The exercise of the clean-up call depends solely on the discretion of the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. (b) The clean-up call is not structured for the purpose of preventing losses from being transferred to investors or of providing credit enhancement to the securitization exposures held by those investors. (c) The exercise of the clean-up call is limited to cases where the balance of the original assets, or of the outstanding securitization exposures held by persons other than the originator, has fallen to 10% or less of the original balance. (vii) The contract relating to the securitization transaction does not contain a provision that sets out a right or condition for terminating the securitization transaction early, except for a provision concerning a clean-up call satisfying all of the conditions listed in (a) through (c) of the preceding item or a provision providing for the termination of the transaction where it is found to be unavoidable. (viii) In a contract relating to a securitization transaction whose original assets include one or more revolving credit facilities, there is no early amortization provision or similar provision that has any of the following effects on the Ultimate Designated Parent Company's interest in those revolving credit facilities: (a) A change that makes the Ultimate Designated Parent Company's interest subordinate to the interests of investors other than the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, in a situation where the interest held by the Ultimate Designated Parent Company ranks senior to, or pari passu with, the interests of those investors. (b) A change that makes the Ultimate Designated Parent Company's interest further subordinate to the interests of the other parties to the securitization transaction, in a situation where the Ultimate Designated Parent Company's interest constitutes a subordinated portion in the securitization transaction. (c) A change that increases the risk of loss on the Ultimate Designated Parent Company's interest by a method other than those in (a) and (b). (ix) The Ultimate Designated Parent Company has not provided credit enhancement, etc. not required by contract.

The provisions of Chapter 3, Section 6 apply mutatis mutandis to the mitigation of credit risk on the original assets in a synthetic securitization transaction, except where it fails to satisfy the conditions listed in item (vi), (viii) or (ix) of the preceding paragraph or any of the following conditions. In this case, in that Section, the term "Ultimate Designated Parent Company adopting the standardized approach" is deemed to be replaced with "Ultimate Designated Parent Company"; in Article 90, item (i), the term "exposure" with "the exposure with the longest residual maturity among the exposures constituting the original asset pool"; in Article 98, item (ii), the phrase "including affiliated companies, etc." with "including affiliated companies, etc. but excluding securitization special purpose entities"; and in Articles 107 and 108, the phrase "residual maturity of the exposure" with "the longest residual maturity among the residual maturities of the exposures constituting the original asset pool". (i) The significant credit risk relating to the original assets has been transferred to a third party. (ii) The contract for the transfer of credit risk on the original assets does not contain any of the provisions listed in (a) through (e) below, or any other similar provision that limits the amount of credit risk transferred: (a) An early amortization provision that has the effect of substantially subordinating the Ultimate Designated Parent Company's interest in a securitization transaction whose original asset pool includes revolving credit facilities; a provision setting a floor on the level at which payments under a guarantee, security interest or protection are not expected to be made even where a credit event occurs; a provision under which the provision of credit enhancement terminates as the credit quality of the exposures constituting the original assets declines; or any other provision similar to these that limits the transfer of credit risk to a significant degree. (b) A provision obliging the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. to exchange assets constituting the original assets for the purpose of improving the average credit quality of the exposures constituting the original assets. (c) A provision under which the consideration for credit enhancement increases as the credit quality of the exposures constituting the original assets declines. (d) A provision for the assumption by the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. of additional first-loss positions or credit enhancement after the execution date of the transaction relating to the credit risk mitigation technique. (e) A provision increasing the payment of benefits to investors, third-party credit enhancement providers or any other person than the Ultimate Designated Parent Company, etc. in accordance with the decline in the credit quality of the exposures constituting the original assets. (iii) An opinion of an attorney, etc. has been obtained to the effect that the contract relating to the credit risk mitigation technique is lawfully and validly formed under relevant laws and is enforceable in accordance with its terms.

An Ultimate Designated Parent Company that is an originator need not calculate the amount of credit risk-weighted assets relating to the original assets where, in an asset-transfer securitization transaction, it does not satisfy all of the conditions listed in each item of paragraph (1), or where, in a synthetic securitization transaction, the provisions of Chapter 3, Section 6 apply mutatis mutandis pursuant to the preceding paragraph, and the securitization transaction has an early amortization provision falling under any of the following cases. (i) A transaction structured with replenishment of the original assets, where replenishment of the original assets has ceased and the Ultimate Designated Parent Company is prohibited, as a result of early amortization, from adding new exposures to the underlying assets. (ii) A securitization transaction having an early amortization provision under which the original assets include revolving credit facilities, which has a structure similar to a term credit facility (meaning a credit facility for which the period and amount are fixed), in which the risk of the original assets does not revert to the Ultimate Designated Parent Company that is the originator, and in which the implementation of early amortization does not substantially subordinate the rights of the Ultimate Designated Parent Company that is the originator. (iii) A case where the Ultimate Designated Parent Company has securitized one or more revolving credit facilities, and investors bear the risk of additional drawdowns by the obligors under those credit facilities even after the commencement of early amortization. (iv) A case where the only early amortization events are events unrelated to the performance of the securitized original assets or the financial condition of the Ultimate Designated Parent Company that is the transferor of those original assets, such as a material change in relevant laws and regulations.

Where the exercise of a clean-up call has the effect of providing credit enhancement, the Ultimate Designated Parent Company is deemed to have provided credit enhancement, etc. not required by contract.
